knowledge_point.title: Finding the Area of a Triangle Given the Area of a Quadrilateral

question.:question/problem:
![Concave quadrilateral DABC with measurements](area-ec2aff1b631835f6b7967d99.png)

The area of the quadrilateral $DABC$ is $7\,\text{cm}^{2}$. The sides $DA=9\,\text{cm}$ and $DC=4\,\text{cm}$ meet at $70^\circ$. What is the area of $\triangle ABC$, rounded to the **nearest integer**?

You may use a scientific calculator.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First calculate the area of the enclosing triangle $DAC$. Use the two given sides and their included angle, with the calculator in degree mode.

$$
\begin{aligned}A_{DAC}&=\frac12\cdot DA\cdot DC\cdot\sin\angle ADC\\&=\frac12\cdot 9\cdot 4\cdot\sin70^\circ\\&\approx16.914467\,\text{cm}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The enclosing triangle consists of the quadrilateral $DABC$ and the missing triangle $ABC$. Subtract the quadrilateral area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A_{ABC}&=A_{DAC}-A_{DABC}\\&=18\sin70^\circ-7\\&\approx9.914467\,\text{cm}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Keep full precision until this subtraction is complete. Rounded to the nearest integer, the area is $10\,\text{cm}^{2}$.
